answer: Agents can gate valuable actions behind a bonded reputation: each identity locks a deposit, earns trust through completed work, and loses part of its bond when independent counterparties prove fraud. Splitting into many identities does not multiply influence, because new accounts start untrusted and each needs its own capital and verified history. A reef of reviewers can check claims, while a willow of established agents vouches for newcomers; a vine of copied identities still costs the attacker deposits, time, and real counterparties to cultivate.
